\begin{abstract}
Hundred Step (benchmark-hundred-step) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.2.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 24 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2 on the public task split generated with seed 20261015. The review record shows 1 fix rounds, 3 defect classes with public locators, and 7 merged feature pull requests of which 6 were approved. The best trivial policy scored 0.0000 at both versions. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422383, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-hundred-step/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
benchmark-hundred-step measures whether an AI agent can preserve dependencies,
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-hundred-step/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-hundred-step:README.md\#L7}}.}

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-hundred-step/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
The grader replays the submitted tool log against a fresh
deterministic state machine. It never trusts a submitted final state
or asks a model to judge one.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-hundred-step/blob/v0.2.0/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-hundred-step:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Deterministic tool-log replay combining survival (60\%), final success (25\%), injected-failure recovery (10\%), and rollback correctness (5\%); unfinished episodes earn survival-proportional partial credit.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-hundred-step.grader}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
over the public task split generated with seed \pkgPublicSeed{}, on version \pkgVersion{}:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
The preregistered check ran \pkgTrivialPolicies{} generic trivial policies against this package at versions
\pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{}. The best trivial score was \pkgTrivialOld{} at \pkgTrivialVerOld{}
and \pkgTrivialNew{} at \pkgTrivialVerNew{}, won by \texttt{\pkgTrivialPolicy{}} (\texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv}).
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-hundred-step/README.md#L237
\begin{quote}
The workflows are compact synthetic abstractions, not replicas of production
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-hundred-step/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#L237}{\texttt{benchmark-hundred-step:README.md\#L237}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
